events.title: RENT: The Musical
events.description:
Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them.

Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship.

This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.

Book, Music, and Lyrics by Jonathan Larson
Musical Arrangements – Steven Skinner
Original Concept/Additional Lyrics – Billy Aronson
Music Supervision and Additional Arrangements – Tim Weil
Dramaturg – Lynn Thomson

The production stars Ned Way as Mark, Jake Smerechniak* as Roger, Branden Mangan* as Collins, Sanju Ebanks as Benny, Deanna Thomas as Joanne, Jordi Viscarri* as Angel, Oriana Fifer as Mimi, and Courtney Lauster* as Maureen.

The ensemble includes: Bryce Antonio, Blaze Dalio, Miclo Cuauhtémoc González, Kelsey LeVie, Alyssa Peters, and Maya Santiago.

The creative team includes:
Director: Joshua M. Feder, Line Producer: Hannah Lee, Choreographer: Hannah Balagot, Music Director: Marc Dalio, Stage Manager: Wilhelm Peters*, Assistant Stage Manager: Jessica Dell Beni, Technical Theater Manager: Emily Clare Gocon, Scenic Designer: Andrea McKenna, Costume Designer: Ariana Michel-Hamblin, Lighting Designer: Zach Pizza, Sound Designer: Kimberly O’Loughlin+, and Props Manager: Cory Seminowicz.

events.description:
Volunteers are needed to help revitalize, beautify, maintain, and improve areas in the cemetery through a variety of gardening, landscaping, and preservation projects. Volunteers will also assist with the tending of our goats and sheep during the summer months. The Historic Jersey City & Harsimus Cemetery was founded in 1829 and was the state’s first private cemetery. The sacred grounds are the eternal resting place of some early notables of Jersey City’s history as well as thousands of soldiers from the Revolutionary & Civil Wars, the War of 1812, the Spanish-American War, WWI and II. Come help preserve history!
Need-To-Know

  • Volunteers will receive a brief orientation upon arrival
  • Free on-site parking is available
  • Please wear closed toed shoes and long pants
  • Sunscreen and bug spray are recommended
  • Protective gloves and eyeglasses are provided
Quick Tips
  • Following specific instructions regarding each task help make everyone have a positive experience

events.title: INSUN PARK & GENERALS
events.description:
ABOUT INSUN PARK & GENERALS

Experience a groundbreaking fusion of rock, Korean traditional music, and mask dance rhythms with Insun Park & Generals. A master of the Gangnyeong Mask Dance, designated as Korea’s National Intangible Heritage, Park leads the quartet, blending her dynamic vocal and dance performances with the talents of Donghyuk Heo (composer/guitar), Hyunmo Yang (drums), Johyun Kim (taepyeongso/flute), and Hahyungki Baek (bass guitar). Together, they create a dynamic blend of ancestral art and contemporary sound, seamlessly merging traditional rhythms with modern rock influences. This ensemble pushes creative boundaries, offering a fresh perspective on Korea’s cultural heritage while making traditional mask dance more accessible to today’s audiences.

Insun Park stands out as one of the few female masters of the Gangnyeong Mask Dance, a tradition historically dominated by men. Renowned for her innovative spirit, she reimagines age-old songs and performance styles to connect with modern audiences. Continuously exploring new creative directions, Park has become a leading force in shaping the future of Korean traditional performing arts.

ABOUT INSUN PARK

Insun Park is a Seoul based mask dancer redefining Korean traditional performance through solo works that bridge ritual, social critique, and contemporary expression. A practitioner of Gangnyeong Talchum, a form of Korea’s National Intangible Heritage, she began training in elementary school and later studied traditional performance at university. Though rooted in a centuries old form, her artistic voice has developed in dialogue with modern urban life.

Traditionally, mask dance (talchum) combined rhythm, song, movement, and dialogue into a comprehensive art form known as yeonhui. While its satire of aristocrats offered audiences catharsis, female and disabled characters were often reduced to stereotypes. Park’s work critically engages this legacy, asking how tradition can be preserved while also responding to contemporary values of gender equity and social inclusion.

Her major solo project, The Purpose of Mask Dance (2021), explores how mask dance can remain socially meaningful today. In this work, female characters lead the narrative as witty, confident, and self determined figures rather than caricatures. Performing as a one woman ensemble, dancing, singing, playing janggu (Korean drum), and shifting roles through masks, Park transforms a historically male and group based genre into a space for personal and social reflection.

In 2023, she expanded this vision through her band Insun Park & Generals, an innovative quintet fusing rock music, Korean traditional sounds, and mask dance rhythms. Led by Park, the ensemble includes Donghyuk Heo (composer and guitar), Hyunmo Yang (drums), Johyun Kim (taepyeongso and flute), and Hahyeonggi Baek (bass guitar). Together, they merge ancestral timbres with modern rock instrumentation, creating a bold, genre crossing soundscape that makes mask dance more accessible to global audiences while expanding its artistic boundaries.

“Insun Park & Generals are unlike anything I’ve ever seen — a joyous and genre-defying explosion of song and dance”

— James Taylor, Program Director, The Cedar Cultural Center

“A stunning voice, charismatic stage presence, and a versatile, ass-kicking rock band… they transfixed the audience from the first note.”

— Bill Bragin, Executive Artistic Director, The Arts Center at NYU Abu Dhabi

“Insun Park had the best stage presence of the night, twirling, jumping, and singing her heart out.”

— NYS Music

“An amalgam of trad folk tunes, ancient shamanistic mask ritual, and punkish rock.”

— World Music Central

“South Korean band Insun Park & Generals delivered a fun yet enigmatic fusion of shamanic ritual folk songs and modern rock… culturally significant and deeply celebratory.”

— Earmilk

events.title: Heels Dance Workshop
events.description:
This one-time, open-level heels workshop blends confident, fluid choreography with the technique to back it up.

Step into your power (literally). This one-time, open-level heels workshop blends confident, fluid choreography with the technique to back it up — no prior heels experience needed, just a willingness to move. Instructor Taylor Green will lead the room through a full combo to a curated track, focusing on posture, hip isolation, and that unapologetic strut that makes heels dance so addictive.

Whether you’re brand new to dancing in heels or already own the floor, come as you are — heels, character shoes, or sneakers to start. All levels welcome. Space is limited, so grab your spot before it fills up.

Instructor Bio:

Taylor’s class is designed to teach dancers the specifics of dancing and performing in a stiletto heel. Class begins with a thorough warmup, weight placement drills in heels, across the floor, and concludes with learning choreography. Taylor’s movement is heavily influenced by street jazz / jazz funk and hip hop grooves combined with the technicality of ballet and traditional jazz training. Class focuses on musicality and performance and is structured to allow students to tap into their own confidence and divine feminine while instilling a sense of community and support.

events.title: Hispanic Heritage Month Film Screening with the Thomas Edison Film Festival
events.description:
HISPANIC HERITAGE MONTH FILM SCREENING “A WAY TO BE TOGETHER”

On Saturday evening October 3rd, 6:30pm, the Thomas Edison Film Festival (TEFF) and the Hoboken Historical Museum present a unique program honoring Hispanic Heritage Month, featuring special guest filmmaker Trina Bardusco.

The evening kicks off with a wine reception at 6:30pm followed by Ms. Bardusco’s inspiring documentary that highlights the power of people and community to come together to make positive change against all odds.  A talk with festival director Jane Steuerwald and Trina Bardusco & Q&A follows the film. The program is free to the public.

“A Way to Be Together” takes place in the New Jersey town of Lambertville, divided by unseen borders, as the Mexican immigrant community steps into the light. Their festival celebration sparks pride and unity—but as fear grows, even joy becomes a radical act of hope.

ABOUT THE FILMMAKER

The filmmaker, Trina Bardusco, is a Venezuelan-American, award-winning storyteller and Fulbright Scholar with a passion for elevating underrepresented voices and crafting bold, culturally rich narratives. Her work lives at the intersection of art, identity, and community.

For over a decade, she brought to life HBO Latino’s acclaimed Habla series, producing sixteen powerful installments that wove together hundreds of personal stories from Latinos across the United States, including celebrities and everyday heroes.

Synopsis

Miss Bellas is a 60–75 minute original music-theater work that explores fame, class division, cultural erasure, and moral responsibility. Set in a dystopian but unsettlingly familiar world, *Miss Bellas* takes place during a lavish annual “Give Back” event hosted by a once working-class performer turned global celebrity. The piece interrogates performative philanthropy, complicity, and the cost of forgetting where you come from.

Blending theatre, live music, bilingual text (English/Spanish), and striking visual design, *Miss Bellas* is both spectacle and critique. It is an immersive experience that asks who pays the price for comfort, celebrity, and silence.

Story

Miss Bellas is at the peak of her fame. She lives inside the Wall, a physical and ideological boundary separating the aristocracy from the impoverished lower class beyond it. Cloistered by her success, Miss Bellas has become ignorant of the realities she once knew. Her annual give-back event, *The Bellas Benefaction*, is ostensibly charitable but has grown increasingly hollow, serving more as a public relations exercise and cash grab than a genuine act of solidarity.

Her long-suffering, emotionally conflicted assistant is caught between two worlds. He remembers Miss Bellas as she once was—a struggling artist deeply connected to her culture. At the same time, he is pressured by a group from outside the Wall to make an example of her, arguing that her fame has made her the perfect symbol of betrayal, privilege, and excess.

As the evening unfolds, what begins as a carefully curated arts showcase transforms into a psychological and moral pressure cooker. The assistant is forced to choose between loyalty, memory, survival, and revolution.

The climax centers on a lethal final confrontation between the assistant and Miss Bellas. For the first time, stripped of artifice, she pleads for her life in Spanish—her native language and the language of her past—desperately attempting to reconnect with the humanity she abandoned. In a final reversal, the assistant does not kill her; instead, he kills his friend and revolutionary leader, Jose.

The show ends with Miss Bellas and the assistant standing together onstage, unchanged in costume and status, forcing the audience to confront the unresolved consequences of that choice.

events.title: Dark Side of the Planetarium Run Rabbit Run
events.description: Some albums are meant to be experienced. Run Rabbit Run—one of the region’s premier Pink Floyd live projects—presents a unique concert performance centered on the legendary ‘The Dark Side of the Moon’ inside the Jennifer Chalsty Planetarium. This concert experience honors the music while taking full advantage of one of New Jersey’s most extraordinary performance spaces!

events.title: Flame (The Experience)
events.description:
In 2021, Afrika Brown published “Flame”, a volume of poetry telling the story of a failed twin flame romance.

For one night, through three acts, “Flame (The Experience)” brings the poetry of the “Flame” alive through a multi-sensory journey told through sight, sound, poetry and movement that explores a failed twin flame relationship that burns to dust.
